discovery: Discovery of exoplanet transits (HD 209458 b) and the first detection of an exoplanet atmosphere

nominees.name: David Charbonneau
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

motivation: In 1999 Charbonneau and Brown, and independently Henry, observed the first transits of an exoplanet, HD 209458 b, across its host star. This was direct proof that the radial-velocity signals were real planets, and it gave the first measurements of a planet's radius and mean density outside the Solar System. In 2002 Charbonneau, Brown and collaborators used Hubble to detect sodium in the planet's atmosphere, the first chemical detection in any exoplanet atmosphere. These precision photometric and spectroscopic measurements, made on modest instruments by researchers who were then young, opened a new field. Transit surveys, from CoRoT and Kepler to TESS, grew out of this work, as did the combination of transits with radial velocities to learn what planets are made of. It also led to today's JWST transmission spectroscopy, which lets us study the atmospheres of other worlds and, eventually, search for signs of life.
